Run The Model Where You Can See Its Progress

Run the launcher from your normal computer Terminal or from the Docker/RStudio Terminal while you can watch the output:

bash scripts/reproduction/run_selected_model_r.sh

The launcher writes selected-model outputs to:

data/processed/selected_model_k6/r/

If a full R selected-model object already exists, the launcher stops before overwriting it. To intentionally rerun the model, set FORCE_RERUN=1:

FORCE_RERUN=1 bash scripts/reproduction/run_selected_model_r.sh

The launcher checks that R CoGAPS was compiled with OpenMP support and sets OMP_NUM_THREADS=4 before starting the run. It then calls scripts/cogaps_run_one_singleprocess_r.R with the selected settings.

The R runner does four important things:

  1. reads data/processed/input/preprocessed_cells_hvg3000.h5ad with zellkonverter;
  2. extracts the normalized expression matrix used by CoGAPS;
  3. builds CogapsParams() with the selected K, seed, iteration count, and sparse-optimization setting; and
  4. saves the full CoGAPS result as cogaps_K6_seed2_iter2000.rds.

The log should show CoGAPS progressing through equilibration and sampling. During equilibration, the sampler moves away from its starting state and toward a region of the model space that fits the data better. During sampling, CoGAPS continues updating the model while collecting the posterior summaries used in the final result.

While the run is active, check for four signs of progress:

  1. the input dimensions and selected settings are printed correctly;
  2. iteration numbers continue to increase;
  3. the run moves from equilibration into sampling; and
  4. the final requested sampling iteration is reached without an error.

Chi-square values do not need to decrease at every sampling update. CoGAPS is a stochastic sampler rather than a monotone optimizer, so small fluctuations during the sampling phase are expected. The diagnostic exports in Stage 4 make the full trace easier to inspect.

The first files to check after this stage are the full selected R CoGAPS object, the metrics JSON, and the checkpoint file. The .rds object is the source for later exports. The metrics JSON provides a compact record of settings, runtime, dimensions, and headline model summaries. The checkpoint is mainly useful for debugging or resuming a run.

Stage 3 checkpoint: The Terminal shows that equilibration and sampling completed, and data/processed/selected_model_k6/r/ contains the full .rds model and metrics JSON. Do not continue to the export stage if the fit ended with an error or stopped before completing sampling.

Stage 4: Create Diagnostic And Analysis Tables

The full model object contains much more information than is practical to display directly in a web page. This stage creates smaller files for two purposes:

  • diagnostic tables summarize the model trace, snapshots, assignments, and posterior uncertainty;
  • analysis tables organize gene weights, cell activities, top genes, and grouped activity summaries into forms that can be inspected with R or Python.

These are not additional model fits. They are different views of the same selected R result.

Export Diagnostics From The Full R Model

The full .rds object is useful, but it is not the easiest format to inspect directly. The diagnostic export script reads the full result and writes smaller files that are easy to plot or summarize:

Rscript scripts/export_cogaps_diagnostics_r.R

This script reads two inputs:

  • data/processed/input/preprocessed_cells_hvg3000.h5ad, so it can check matrix orientation and names; and
  • data/processed/selected_model_k6/r/cogaps_K6_seed2_iter2000.rds, the full selected R CoGAPS result.

The script extracts four model matrices from the CoGAPS object:

  • the gene-loading matrix, often called A, where rows are genes and columns are patterns;
  • the cell-activity matrix, often called P, where rows are cells and columns are patterns;
  • the gene-loading standard-deviation matrix; and
  • the cell-activity standard-deviation matrix.

It also reads CoGAPS metadata: chi-square trace values, atom-count traces, snapshots, pump statistics, mean pattern assignment summaries, run parameters, and runtime metadata.

The main outputs are:

Diagnostic output What it contains Where it is used
cogaps_K6_seed2_iter2000.trace.csv Chi-square and atom-count traces across the run. Convergence and stability checks.
cogaps_K6_seed2_iter2000.snapshot_summary.csv Comparisons between saved intermediate sampler states and the final selected result. Snapshot-based stability checks.
cogaps_K6_seed2_iter2000.pattern_uncertainty_summary.csv Per-pattern uncertainty summaries based on posterior standard-deviation matrices. Posterior uncertainty interpretation.
cogaps_K6_seed2_iter2000.pump_stat.tsv.gz
cogaps_K6_seed2_iter2000.mean_pattern_assignment.tsv.gz 		Pump and mean pattern-assignment diagnostics, when those diagnostics are present in the saved result. Pattern assignment and diagnostic record.
cogaps_K6_seed2_iter2000.diagnostics.json Compact diagnostic record with dimensions, parameter settings, trace summaries, snapshot counts, and metadata fields. Run-level reporting and checks.

These files are the bridge between model fitting and model diagnosis. They let you check convergence, snapshots, uncertainty, and runtime without opening a large R object by hand.

Export Compact R Tables For Analysis

The next export script turns the same full R result into the matrices and summaries used throughout the main analysis sections:

Rscript scripts/export_lightweight_cogaps_derivatives_r.R

This script again reads the prepared PBMC .h5ad file and the selected R .rds object. It then creates the tables that the main analysis uses.

The export script creates three kinds of files:

Output family Output files How the files are used
Model matrices pattern_gene_weights.tsv.gz
pattern_cell_activities.tsv.gz
pattern_gene_weight_sd.tsv.gz
pattern_cell_activity_sd.tsv.gz 		Gene weights identify which genes define each pattern. Cell activities identify where each pattern is used across cells. Posterior SD matrices support uncertainty summaries.
Cell activities joined to metadata pattern_cell_activities_with_metadata.csv.gz Joins each cell’s pattern activities to barcode, condition, donor/replicate, annotated PBMC identity, and UMAP coordinates. This is what lets later sections compare pattern activity with stimulation, cell identity, donor structure, and UMAP location.
Pattern-level summaries pattern_top_genes.csv
pattern_correlations.csv
pattern_activity_by_celltype_condition.csv
pattern_activity_by_replicate_condition.csv
pattern_summary.csv 		Ranks top genes, measures association with stimulation, summarizes activity by PBMC identity and donor, and gathers compact pattern evidence for tables and figures.

These files are not separate models. They are smaller views of the selected R model, reshaped so you can inspect one kind of evidence at a time.

Check The Exported Tables In R Or Python

The export scripts are written in R because they read the full R CoGAPS object. Once the CSV and compressed TSV files have been created, you can inspect them in either language.

  • R
  • Python
pattern_summary_r <- readr::read_csv(
  "data/processed/selected_model_k6/r/pattern_summary.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

pattern_summary_r |>
  dplyr::select(
    pattern,
    corr_with_stim,
    dominant_cell_type,
    top_genes_top8
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()
import pandas as pd

pattern_summary_py = pd.read_csv(
    "data/processed/selected_model_k6/r/pattern_summary.csv"
)

pattern_summary_py[
    [
        "pattern",
        "corr_with_stim",
        "dominant_cell_type",
        "top_genes_top8",
    ]
]

Both snippets read the same R-selected-model summary. The check should return one row for each of the six patterns and retain the columns needed to connect stimulation association, cell identity, and top genes.

Stage 4 checkpoint: The trace, uncertainty, gene-weight, cell-activity, top-gene, and pattern-summary files are present. The pattern summary contains six rows, and the matrices retain matching gene, cell, and pattern labels.

Stage 5: Rebuild Directionality And Figures

The selected-model exports show which genes have high CoGAPS weights and where each pattern is active. They do not show whether a high-weight gene increases or decreases after IFN-beta stimulation. This stage adds that expression-direction evidence and rebuilds the figures that display the combined results.

Rebuild Directionality Evidence

The R model export tells you which genes have high CoGAPS weights. It does not tell you whether those genes are higher after IFN-beta stimulation. Directionality is rebuilt with a separate expression-contrast script. Choose the command that matches the selected-model outputs you are rebuilding.

  • R
  • Python
Rscript scripts/pattern_directionality_analysis_r.R
/opt/cogaps-venv/bin/python scripts/pattern_directionality_analysis.py

This script uses the prepared expression values, selected model top genes, donor labels, condition labels, and annotated PBMC identities. It builds pseudobulk summaries and compares IFN-beta-stimulated aliquots with matched control aliquots.

The main outputs are:

Directionality output What it contains Why it matters
pattern_gene_directionality_global.csv Gene-level IFN-beta versus control contrasts across all cells. Checks whether top genes rise or fall overall.
pattern_gene_directionality_by_celltype.csv Gene-level contrasts within annotated PBMC identities. Checks whether direction is consistent or cell-type-specific.
pattern_direction_summary.csv One row per pattern summarizing how many top genes are higher or lower after stimulation. Supports pattern-level direction interpretation.
pseudobulk_counts_global.csv
pseudobulk_counts_by_celltype.csv 		Support files showing how many observations contributed to the expression summaries. Helps check whether a contrast is based on enough cells.
pattern_gene_directionality_heatmap.png Compact visual summary of directionality across patterns and cell types. Useful for quick review after rerunning the directionality script.

The directionality step is part of the evidence chain because CoGAPS weights and expression fold-changes answer different questions. A gene can strongly define a pattern and still move in either direction after stimulation. The case study therefore interprets gene weights and expression direction together.

Check The R Output Folder

After running the R fit and export scripts, inspect the output folder:

find data/processed/selected_model_k6/r -maxdepth 1 -type f | sort

You should see the full selected model, diagnostic files, lightweight matrices, activity summaries, top-gene tables, and directionality summaries. If a later case-study section cannot find a file, start by checking whether it appears in this folder and whether it was regenerated after the latest model run.

Regenerate The Displayed Figures

Most displayed figures are built from processed evidence tables rather than directly from a live model fit. That separation makes it possible to update a visualization without waiting for CoGAPS to run again.

Regenerate the shared selected-model figures with:

/opt/cogaps-venv/bin/python scripts/build_selected_k6_figures.py

The script writes figures under data/processed/figures/ and updates selected display copies under img/. Figures generated directly by R and Python code chunks are refreshed when the complete Quarto page is rendered:

quarto render

Before interpreting a rebuilt figure, confirm that its source table was regenerated from the same selected-model output. A newly rendered image does not correct an older source table by itself.

Stage 5 checkpoint: Directionality tables and pseudobulk support files are present for the selected output, the expected figures have been regenerated, and the Quarto render completes without missing-file errors.

Stage 6: Confirm The Reproduction

A successful script exit is necessary, but it is not the only check. Confirm that the regenerated files still represent the intended dataset and model.

Check Expected result Why it matters
Prepared data 24,673 cells, 3,000 genes, and the required condition, donor, cell-type, and UMAP fields Confirms that CoGAPS received the intended cells, genes, and metadata.
Selected settings K = 6, seed 2, 2,000 iterations per phase, and sparse optimization enabled Confirms that the regenerated model matches the selected specification.
Pattern structure Six gene-weight and cell-activity columns with aligned pattern labels Confirms that the compact exports describe the complete selected model.
Diagnostics Trace, snapshot, uncertainty, metrics, and available pump files are present for R Confirms that the evidence needed to evaluate the R run was exported.
Directionality Global, cell-type, paired, and pseudobulk support tables are present Confirms that expression direction can be interpreted separately from CoGAPS weights.
Display files Figures were rebuilt after their source tables Confirms that the page displays the current evidence.

The checks below summarize the selected-model folder from either language. They do not decide whether the biological interpretation is correct; they confirm that the expected evidence files are available and internally complete.

  • R
  • Python
r_dir <- "data/processed/selected_model_k6/r"

r_check <- data.frame(
  check = c(
    "pattern rows",
    "trace file",
    "uncertainty file",
    "directionality file",
    "full R model"
  ),
  value = c(
    nrow(readr::read_csv(file.path(r_dir, "pattern_summary.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)),
    file.exists(file.path(r_dir, "cogaps_K6_seed2_iter2000.trace.csv")),
    file.exists(file.path(r_dir, "cogaps_K6_seed2_iter2000.pattern_uncertainty_summary.csv")),
    file.exists(file.path(r_dir, "pattern_gene_directionality_global.csv")),
    file.exists(file.path(r_dir, "cogaps_K6_seed2_iter2000.rds"))
  )
)

knitr::kable(r_check)
from pathlib import Path
import pandas as pd

py_dir = Path("data/processed/selected_model_k6/python")

py_check = pd.DataFrame(
    {
        "check": [
            "pattern rows",
            "metrics file",
            "directionality file",
            "full Python-compatible model",
        ],
        "value": [
            len(pd.read_csv(py_dir / "pattern_summary.csv")),
            (py_dir / "cogaps_K6_seed2_iter2000.metrics.json").exists(),
            (py_dir / "pattern_gene_directionality_global.csv").exists(),
            (py_dir / "cogaps_K6_seed2_iter2000.h5ad").exists(),
        ],
    }
)

py_check

The R table should report six pattern rows and TRUE for every expected file. The Python table should also report six pattern rows and TRUE for its available output files. The Python list is shorter because the Python-compatible run does not expose the same snapshot and pump diagnostics as the selected R run.

If a regenerated value differs, stop before replacing the included evidence. Review the preprocessing record, matrix orientation, model settings, random seed, runtime environment, and export logs to identify where the difference entered the workflow.

Stage 6 checkpoint: The structural checks pass, the expected files are current, and any differences from the included result have been explained before the regenerated files are used for interpretation.

Optional Extension: Rebuild The Python-Compatible Model

Use this extension if you want to recreate the Python-compatible output shown in the Python tabs. It addresses the same biological questions as the selected R model, but its pattern numbers and available diagnostics are implementation-specific. In the included outputs, the R run labels the IFN-associated signal Pattern4, while the Python-compatible output labels the corresponding signal Pattern5.

The Python-compatible fit requires the dense genes-by-cells input:

data/processed/input/cogaps_input_genesxcells_hvg3000_float64.h5ad

Run the launcher in a visible Terminal:

bash scripts/reproduction/run_selected_model_python.sh

The result is written under data/processed/selected_model_k6/python/. If a full result already exists, the launcher stops before replacing it. Use FORCE_RERUN=1 only when you have intentionally chosen to replace that result:

FORCE_RERUN=1 bash scripts/reproduction/run_selected_model_python.sh

The Python-compatible launcher uses nSnapshots = 0 because its snapshot-conversion route does not provide the same reliable diagnostic export used by R. After model fitting completes, create the compact tables and directionality summaries:

/opt/cogaps-venv/bin/python scripts/export_lightweight_cogaps_derivatives.py
/opt/cogaps-venv/bin/python scripts/pattern_directionality_analysis.py

Check the Python-compatible folder with the Python tab in Stage 6. Compare biological evidence by cell activity, top genes, condition association, and cell-type structure rather than assuming that the same pattern number must be recovered in both implementations.

Python extension checkpoint: The full H5AD result, metrics JSON, six-row pattern summary, gene-weight and cell-activity files, and directionality tables are present. Pattern labels may differ from R, but the evidence used to match corresponding signals should be available.

Optional Extension: Understand How The Rank Sweep Was Run

The full rank sweep supports the choice of K = 6, but it is not part of local reproduction. The sweep used many CoGAPS runs across candidate ranks, seeds, and iteration counts. That is cluster work, not work you need to do on a local computer.

The useful idea is not the exact cluster command. The useful idea is the design pattern: build one reproducible input, write an explicit table of model runs, let the scheduler run one row at a time, and aggregate the completed runs into evidence tables before choosing one model for interpretation.

The included model-selection summaries live under:

data/processed/k_selection/

Those files are used in Data Import to evaluate model resolution. They connect the completed sweep runs with the model-choice tables shown in the case study.

For transparency, the repository includes portable copies of the scripts that prepared the sweep inputs, ran individual model fits, aggregated completed runs, and summarized candidate models:

scripts/reproduction/hpc_sweep/

Read the sweep as a sequence of jobs. A Slurm launch script submits work to the cluster, while the Python script named in the same row performs the data preparation, model fitting, or summarization.

Sweep stage Launcher or script What it does What you check afterward
Prepare cache and jobs prep_cogaps_cache_and_jobs_rhino_light.sbatch
cogaps_prep_cache.py
make_cogaps_jobs_tsv.py 		The Slurm launch script activates the cluster environment, preprocesses the PBMC object once, and writes a headerless jobs table. Each row of the jobs table is one model setting: K, seed, and iteration count. The cache folder should contain the prepared cells-by-genes object, the genes-by-cells CoGAPS input, and the preprocessing JSON. The jobs table should have the expected number of rows.
Run one model per array task cogaps_sweep_array_singleprocess_rhino_light.sbatch
cogaps_run_one_singleprocess.py 		Each Slurm array task uses SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID to read one row from the jobs table. It passes that row to the single-run PyCoGAPS script, which fits one model and writes model output plus a metrics JSON. The runs/ folder should fill with one model object and one metrics file per completed row. The logs/ folder should show progress and failures for individual tasks.
Aggregate completed runs aggregate_cogaps_results_rhino_light.sbatch
cogaps_aggregate_results.py 		The aggregation script reads completed metrics files, checks sweep coverage, summarizes runtime and IFN-pattern evidence by K, and writes report-ready summary files. The output folder should contain per_run_metrics.csv, summary_by_K.csv, and report.md. These files are the starting point for model-resolution evidence.
Summarize candidate models phase2_candidate_model_interpretation.py This post-processing script compares selected candidate models more closely. It summarizes pattern activity, top genes, cell-type and condition structure, and cross-model pattern matching. The key output files include candidate_pattern_summary.csv, candidate_top_genes.csv, activity-by-cell-type summaries, and cross-model match tables.
Check high-rank behavior submit_phase3_highk_2000_rhino.sh
phase3_highk_fragmentation_analysis.py 		The helper submits a separate high-K array using the same single-run and aggregation launch scripts. The fragmentation script then checks whether higher ranks improve the IFN evidence or mostly split existing structure. The high-rank summary should show whether large K values improve stability enough to justify their runtime. In this case study, they did not replace the selected lower-rank model.

Initial Sweep Order

The first sweep pass used the same cached PBMC input for all model runs. That matters because the rank comparison should not mix changes in K with changes in preprocessing. The preparation job therefore runs once before the array is submitted.

# Stage 1: build the cached PBMC input and the jobs table.
sbatch prep_cogaps_cache_and_jobs_rhino_light.sbatch

The preparation job calls these two Python programs:

python3 cogaps_prep_cache.py \
  --input-h5ad kang_counts_25k.h5ad \
  --outdir results_cogaps_singleprocess_hpc \
  --min-cells 3 \
  --target-sum 10000 \
  --n-top-genes 3000 \
  --hvg-flavor seurat_v3

python3 make_cogaps_jobs_tsv.py \
  --k-grid 7,9,11,13 \
  --seeds 1,2,3,4,5 \
  --iters 2000,10000,20000 \
  --out results_cogaps_singleprocess_hpc/jobs.tsv

The jobs table is intentionally simple. It has no header; each line is a tab-separated K, seed, and iteration count. The initial sweep table had 60 rows: four candidate ranks, five seeds, and three iteration settings.

# Stage 2: submit one Slurm array task per row in jobs.tsv.
OUTDIR=results_cogaps_singleprocess_hpc
JOBS_TSV=${OUTDIR}/jobs.tsv
N=$(wc -l < "${JOBS_TSV}")

sbatch --export=ALL,OUTDIR="${OUTDIR}",JOBS_TSV="${JOBS_TSV}" \
  --array=0-$((N-1))%15 \
  cogaps_sweep_array_singleprocess_rhino_light.sbatch

The %15 limit is a concurrency cap. It allows at most 15 array tasks to run at the same time. Each task is still one single-process CoGAPS run; the cluster parallelism comes from running many independent rows of the jobs table.

Each array task reads one row from jobs.tsv and calls:

python3 cogaps_run_one_singleprocess.py \
  --cogaps-input-h5ad results_cogaps_singleprocess_hpc/cache/cogaps_input_genesxcells_hvg3000_float64.h5ad \
  --outdir results_cogaps_singleprocess_hpc \
  --k "${K}" \
  --seed "${SEED}" \
  --n-iter "${NITER}" \
  --stim-label "stim" \
  --top-genes 50 \
  --use-sparse-opt \
  --blas-threads "${NTHREADS}" \
  --cogaps-threads "${NTHREADS}"

That single-run script writes one saved result and one metrics JSON for the row it received. The metrics file is important because it records the runtime, selected IFN-associated pattern, IFN correlation, top genes, and status for that model.

# Stage 3: aggregate after the array completes.
sbatch --dependency=afterok:<ARRAY_JOB_ID> \
  aggregate_cogaps_results_rhino_light.sbatch

After the model jobs finish, the aggregation job calls:

python3 cogaps_aggregate_results.py \
  --outdir results_cogaps_singleprocess_hpc \
  --k-grid 7,9,11,13 \
  --seeds 1,2,3,4,5 \
  --iters 2000,10000,20000 \
  --top-genes 50 \
  --preprocessed-h5ad results_cogaps_singleprocess_hpc/cache/preprocessed_cells_hvg3000.h5ad \
  --no-umap

Aggregation is where individual model runs become model-selection evidence. The script does not choose a model by looking at one run in isolation. It reads the available metrics files, checks whether expected combinations are missing, summarizes performance by candidate rank, and writes the tables that can be inspected in the case study.

Lower-Rank And Longer-Run Follow-Ups

The first sweep made it clear that the lower end of the rank grid needed closer inspection. The follow-up jobs reused the same array runner, but with new jobs tables:

Follow-up Jobs table What varied Why it was run
Lower-rank sweep jobs_phase1_lowerk.tsv K = 2 through K = 7, seeds 1-5, 2,000 iterations. Ask whether a smaller number of patterns could still recover the IFN-associated signal.
Longer lower-rank sweep jobs_phase1b_lowerk_long.tsv K = 4, 5, and 6, seeds 1-5, 10,000 and 20,000 iterations. Check whether lower-rank candidates stayed stable when the model was allowed to run longer.
Candidate-model interpretation phase2_candidate_model_interpretation.py Post-processing of candidate models rather than a new CoGAPS fit. Compare pattern-level biology, top genes, activity structure, and cross-model matching before selecting the case-study model.

These follow-ups are why the case study does not treat the original rank grid as the final word. The lower-rank and longer-run summaries provide the evidence that K = 6 is a better compromise for this PBMC IFN-beta dataset than a more compressed K = 4 model or a higher-rank model.

High-K Extension

The high-rank extension asked the opposite question: could much larger ranks reveal useful structure that the lower-rank candidates missed? It used candidate values from K = 14 to K = 80 at 2,000 iterations:

bash submit_phase3_highk_2000_rhino.sh

That helper prepares the high-K jobs table, makes the Slurm launch files available on Rhino, submits the array, and then submits the aggregation job after the array succeeds. The same single-run Python script performs the model fit for each row.

The high-K jobs table used:

K_GRID=14,20,26,32,38,44,50,56,62,68,74,80
SEEDS=1,2,3,4,5
ITERS=2000

After those runs, phase3_highk_fragmentation_analysis.py summarized whether high ranks improved the IFN-associated evidence or mostly split signal across extra patterns. The current model decision uses the high-K extension as a check against missing a clearly better high-rank model; it does not make high-K reruns part of local reproduction.

Cluster note

Do not run the Slurm commands while working through the main analysis. They are included so you can see how the sweep summaries were produced and how you might design a similar sweep for your own project. Cluster paths, account settings, conda environments, partitions, memory, walltime, and software activation commands must be adapted to the cluster where you run them.

The important design idea is transferable even if the cluster commands are not. A sweep should record candidate ranks, seeds, iteration counts, runtime, pattern summaries, stability evidence, and enough per-run metadata to let the model choice be reviewed later. For this case study, the reviewed summaries under data/processed/k_selection/ are the evidence used in the model-choice checkpoint.

Script Library: Read The Complete Workflow

The complete scripts show every operation used by the reproduction workflow. The command examples above show how to launch the major stages. The dropdowns below show the script bodies in the same order: path setup, preprocessing, model fitting, diagnostics, table exports, directionality, figure building, and the optional rank sweep.

Opening a dropdown displays code but does not run it. Shell launchers such as run_selected_model_r.sh and run_selected_model_python.sh set paths and options before calling R or Python. The dropdowns show the underlying R or Python programs so you can inspect the operations that produce each output.

1. R path helper

scripts/helpers/case_study_paths.R
Defines the R file paths used by analysis chunks and reproduction checks. 

# Shared setup for the CoGAPS PBMC case study.
# Source this file before running later case-study chunks.

find_project_root_r <- function(start = getwd()) {
  path <- normalizePath(start, winslash = "/", mustWork = FALSE)
  repeat {
    if (file.exists(file.path(path, "index.qmd")) && dir.exists(file.path(path, "data"))) {
      return(path)
    }
    parent <- dirname(path)
    if (identical(parent, path)) {
      stop("Could not locate the case-study project root.")
    }
    path <- parent
  }
}

resolve_first_existing_r <- function(...) {
  candidates <- c(...)
  for (candidate in candidates) {
    if (file.exists(candidate)) {
      return(candidate)
    }
  }
  candidates[[1]]
}

INPUT_DIR_R <- file.path(PROCESSED_DIR_R, "input")

pattern_columns_r <- function(x) {
  pats <- grep("^Pattern_?[0-9]+$", x, value = TRUE)
  pats[order(as.integer(sub("^Pattern_?", "", pats)))]
}

canonicalize_pattern_names_r <- function(x) {
  sub("^Pattern_?([0-9]+)$", "Pattern\\1", x)
}

top_genes_from_matrix_r <- function(matrix, pattern, n = 15) {
  ordered <- sort(matrix[, pattern], decreasing = TRUE)
  ordered <- head(ordered, n)
  tibble::tibble(
    gene = names(ordered),
    weight = unname(ordered)
  )
}

load_lightweight_pattern_matrices_r <- function(weights_path, activities_path) {
  A <- readr::read_tsv(weights_path, show_col_types = FALSE) |>
    tibble::column_to_rownames("gene") |>
    as.data.frame(check.names = FALSE)
  P <- readr::read_tsv(activities_path, show_col_types = FALSE) |>
    tibble::column_to_rownames("cell_barcode") |>
    as.data.frame(check.names = FALSE)
  colnames(A) <- canonicalize_pattern_names_r(colnames(A))
  colnames(P) <- canonicalize_pattern_names_r(colnames(P))
  list(A = A, P = P)
}

"""Shared setup for the CoGAPS PBMC case study.

Import this module before running later case-study chunks.
"""

from pathlib import Path

import anndata as ad
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy import sparse


def find_project_root(start: Path) -> Path:
    for path in [start, *start.parents]:
        if (path / "index.qmd").exists() and (path / "data").exists():
            return path
    raise FileNotFoundError("Could not locate the case-study project root.")


def resolve_first_existing(*candidates: Path) -> Path:
    for candidate in candidates:
        if candidate.exists():
            return candidate
    return candidates[0]

def pattern_columns(df: pd.DataFrame) -> list[str]:
    return sorted(
        [c for c in df.columns if str(c).startswith("Pattern")],
        key=lambda value: int(str(value).replace("Pattern", "")),
    )


def top_genes_from_matrix(matrix: pd.DataFrame, pattern: str, n: int = 15) -> pd.DataFrame:
    top = matrix[pattern].sort_values(ascending=False).head(n)
    top_df = top.rename("weight").reset_index()
    top_df.columns = ["gene", "weight"]
    return top_df


def load_lightweight_pattern_matrices(weights_path: Path, activities_path: Path) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    A = pd.read_csv(weights_path, sep="\t", compression="gzip").set_index("gene")
    P = pd.read_csv(activities_path, sep="\t", compression="gzip").set_index("cell_barcode")
    return A, P


def build_cogaps_input(preprocessed_cells: ad.AnnData) -> ad.AnnData:
    cogaps_input = preprocessed_cells.T.copy()
    X = cogaps_input.X.toarray() if sparse.issparse(cogaps_input.X) else cogaps_input.X
    cogaps_input.X = np.asarray(X, dtype=np.float64)
    cogaps_input.var = preprocessed_cells.obs.copy()
    cogaps_input.var_names = preprocessed_cells.obs_names.copy()
    cogaps_input.obs = preprocessed_cells.var.copy()
    cogaps_input.obs_names = preprocessed_cells.var_names.copy()
    return cogaps_input


__all__ = [
    "find_project_root",
    "resolve_first_existing",
    "pattern_columns",
    "top_genes_from_matrix",
    "load_lightweight_pattern_matrices",
    "build_cogaps_input",
    *[name for name in globals() if name.isupper()],
]
3. Rebuild the prepared PBMC dataset

scripts/reproduction/prepare_preprocessed_hvg3000.py
Reads the larger source AnnData file, filters genes, normalizes/log-transforms expression, selects highly variable genes, and writes the prepared inputs. 

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Recreate the prepared PBMC dataset from a larger source H5AD file.

This script is for the optional full reproduction path. The main learner path
uses the prepared H5AD and lightweight CoGAPS outputs already included with the
case study.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

import anndata as ad
import numpy as np
from scipy import sparse


def parse_args() -> argparse.Namespace:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument(
        "--source-h5ad",
        type=Path,
        default=Path("data/source/kang_counts_25k.h5ad"),
        help="Larger source counts H5AD file.",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--out-h5ad",
        type=Path,
        default=Path("data/processed/input/preprocessed_cells_hvg3000.h5ad"),
        help="Prepared cells x genes H5AD file.",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--cogaps-input-h5ad",
        type=Path,
        default=Path("data/processed/input/cogaps_input_genesxcells_hvg3000_float64.h5ad"),
        help="Optional dense genes x cells PyCoGAPS input.",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--config-json",
        type=Path,
        default=Path("data/processed/input/preprocess_config_hvg3000.json"),
        help="Preprocessing settings record.",
    )
    parser.add_argument("--min-cells", type=int, default=3)
    parser.add_argument("--target-sum", type=float, default=10000.0)
    parser.add_argument("--n-top-genes", type=int, default=3000)
    parser.add_argument("--hvg-flavor", default="seurat_v3")
    return parser.parse_args()


def build_cogaps_input(preprocessed_cells: ad.AnnData) -> ad.AnnData:
    """Convert cells x genes AnnData into a dense genes x cells file."""
    cogaps_input = preprocessed_cells.T.copy()
    X = cogaps_input.X.toarray() if sparse.issparse(cogaps_input.X) else cogaps_input.X
    cogaps_input.X = np.asarray(X, dtype=np.float64)
    cogaps_input.var = preprocessed_cells.obs.copy()
    cogaps_input.var_names = preprocessed_cells.obs_names.astype(str).copy()
    cogaps_input.obs = preprocessed_cells.var.copy()
    cogaps_input.obs_names = preprocessed_cells.var_names.astype(str).copy()
    return cogaps_input


def main() -> None:
    args = parse_args()

    try:
        import scanpy as sc
    except ImportError as exc:
        raise SystemExit(
            "This full-reproduction preprocessing script requires scanpy. "
            "Use the validated case-study image or install scanpy in your environment."
        ) from exc

    if not args.source_h5ad.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(
            f"Source H5AD not found: {args.source_h5ad}. "
            "Download or mount the larger source file before running this script."
        )

    adata = ad.read_h5ad(args.source_h5ad)

    if "counts" not in adata.layers:
        adata.layers["counts"] = adata.X.copy()

    sc.pp.filter_genes(adata, min_cells=args.min_cells)
    sc.pp.normalize_total(adata, target_sum=args.target_sum)
    sc.pp.log1p(adata)
    sc.pp.highly_variable_genes(
        adata,
        n_top_genes=args.n_top_genes,
        flavor=args.hvg_flavor,
        layer="counts",
        subset=False,
    )

    if "highly_variable" not in adata.var:
        raise RuntimeError("HVG selection did not create adata.var['highly_variable'].")

    adata_hvg = adata[:, adata.var["highly_variable"].to_numpy()].copy()

    args.out_h5ad.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    args.cogaps_input_h5ad.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    args.config_json.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    adata_hvg.write_h5ad(args.out_h5ad)

    cogaps_input = build_cogaps_input(adata_hvg)
    cogaps_input.write_h5ad(args.cogaps_input_h5ad)

    config = {
        "raw_h5ad": args.source_h5ad.name,
        "min_cells": args.min_cells,
        "target_sum": args.target_sum,
        "hvg_flavor": args.hvg_flavor,
        "n_top_genes": args.n_top_genes,
        "created_at": datetime.now(timezone.utc).replace(microsecond=0).isoformat(),
        "prepared_h5ad": str(args.out_h5ad),
        "cogaps_input_h5ad": str(args.cogaps_input_h5ad),
    }
    args.config_json.write_text(json.dumps(config, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")

    print(f"Wrote prepared PBMC dataset: {args.out_h5ad}")
    print(f"Wrote CoGAPS input: {args.cogaps_input_h5ad}")
    print(f"Wrote preprocessing record: {args.config_json}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env Rscript

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(optparse)
  library(jsonlite)
  library(zellkonverter)
  library(CoGAPS)
  library(SummarizedExperiment)
})

pattern_columns <- function(x) {
  pats <- grep("^Pattern_?[0-9]+$", x, value = TRUE)
  pats[order(as.integer(sub("^Pattern_?", "", pats)))]
}

canonicalize_pattern_names <- function(x) {
  sub("^Pattern_?([0-9]+)$", "Pattern\\1", x)
}

`%||%` <- function(x, y) if (is.null(x)) y else x

ensure_pattern_matrix_orientation <- function(mat, expected_rows, expected_names) {
  if (is.null(dim(mat))) {
    stop("Expected a 2D matrix.")
  }

  if (nrow(mat) != expected_rows && ncol(mat) == expected_rows) {
    mat <- t(mat)
  }

  if (nrow(mat) != expected_rows) {
    stop(sprintf("Unexpected matrix shape. Expected %d rows, got %d.", expected_rows, nrow(mat)))
  }

  if (is.null(rownames(mat))) {
    rownames(mat) <- expected_names
  }

  mat
}

write_metrics <- function(path, metrics) {
  write_json(metrics, path = path, auto_unbox = TRUE, pretty = TRUE)
}

option_list <- list(
  make_option("--preprocessed-h5ad", type = "character", dest = "preprocessed_h5ad", help = "Processed cells x genes AnnData (.h5ad)"),
  make_option("--outdir", type = "character", default = "data/results_r", help = "Output directory [default %default]"),
  make_option("--k", type = "integer", help = "Number of patterns"),
  make_option("--seed", type = "integer", help = "Random seed"),
  make_option("--n-iter", type = "integer", dest = "n_iter", help = "Number of iterations"),
  make_option("--top-genes", type = "integer", dest = "top_genes", default = 50, help = "Top genes used for summary metrics [default %default]"),
  make_option("--stim-label", type = "character", dest = "stim_label", default = "stim", help = "Stimulated condition label [default %default]"),
  make_option("--cogaps-threads", type = "integer", dest = "cogaps_threads", default = 1, help = "Threads passed to CoGAPS [default %default]"),
  make_option("--async-updates", action = "store_true", dest = "asynchronous_updates", default = TRUE, help = "Enable CoGAPS asynchronous updates [default]"),
  make_option("--sync-updates", action = "store_false", dest = "asynchronous_updates", help = "Disable CoGAPS asynchronous updates"),
  make_option("--output-frequency", type = "integer", dest = "output_frequency", default = 1000, help = "Trace output frequency passed to CoGAPS [default %default]"),
  make_option("--checkpoint-interval", type = "integer", dest = "checkpoint_interval", default = 0, help = "Iterations between checkpoint writes [default %default]"),
  make_option("--checkpoint-outfile", type = "character", dest = "checkpoint_outfile", default = NULL, help = "Checkpoint output file path [default auto in outdir when checkpointing is enabled]"),
  make_option("--n-snapshots", type = "integer", dest = "n_snapshots", default = 0, help = "Snapshots to capture per enabled phase [default %default]"),
  make_option("--snapshot-phase", type = "character", dest = "snapshot_phase", default = "sampling", help = "Snapshot phase: sampling, equilibration, or all [default %default]"),
  make_option("--take-pump-samples", action = "store_true", dest = "take_pump_samples", default = FALSE, help = "Capture pump statistics and mean pattern assignment diagnostics"),
  make_option("--quiet", action = "store_false", dest = "messages", default = TRUE, help = "Suppress CoGAPS status messages"),
  make_option("--use-sparse-opt", action = "store_true", dest = "use_sparse_opt", default = TRUE, help = "Enable sparseOptimization [default]"),
  make_option("--no-sparse-opt", action = "store_false", dest = "use_sparse_opt", help = "Disable sparseOptimization"),
  make_option("--force-rerun", action = "store_true", default = FALSE, help = "Ignore successful cached outputs and rerun")
)

opt <- parse_args(OptionParser(option_list = option_list))

if (is.null(opt$preprocessed_h5ad) || is.null(opt$k) || is.null(opt$seed) || is.null(opt$n_iter)) {
  stop("Missing required arguments. Use --help for details.")
}

outdir <- normalizePath(opt$outdir, winslash = "/", mustWork = FALSE)
dir.create(outdir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

tag <- sprintf("K%d_seed%d_iter%d", opt$k, opt$seed, opt$n_iter)
result_path <- file.path(outdir, sprintf("cogaps_%s.rds", tag))
metrics_path <- file.path(outdir, sprintf("cogaps_%s.metrics.json", tag))
checkpoint_path <- opt$checkpoint_outfile
if (is.null(checkpoint_path) || identical(checkpoint_path, "")) {
  checkpoint_path <- file.path(outdir, sprintf("cogaps_%s.checkpoint.out", tag))
}

if (file.exists(result_path) && file.exists(metrics_path) && !isTRUE(opt$force_rerun)) {
  prior_metrics <- tryCatch(fromJSON(metrics_path), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (!is.null(prior_metrics) && identical(prior_metrics$status, "ok")) {
    message(sprintf("[CACHE] status=ok; skipping %s", tag))
    quit(save = "no", status = 0)
  }
}

status <- "ok"
err_txt <- NULL
t0 <- Sys.time()

tryCatch({
  sce <- zellkonverter::readH5AD(opt$preprocessed_h5ad, reader = "R")
  data_matrix <- SummarizedExperiment::assay(sce, "X")
  data_matrix <- as.matrix(data_matrix)
  openmp_support <- compiledWithOpenMPSupport()

  if (opt$cogaps_threads > 1 && !openmp_support) {
    stop(
      paste(
        "This CoGAPS build does not report OpenMP support, so requesting",
        sprintf("nThreads=%d", opt$cogaps_threads),
        "would silently fall back to a single-threaded run.",
        "Rebuild the runtime with OpenMP-enabled CoGAPS before benchmarking multithreading."
      )
    )
  }

  params <- CogapsParams(
    nPatterns = opt$k,
    nIterations = opt$n_iter,
    seed = opt$seed,
    sparseOptimization = isTRUE(opt$use_sparse_opt)
  )
  params@takePumpSamples <- isTRUE(opt$take_pump_samples)

  set.seed(opt$seed)
  result <- CoGAPS(
    data_matrix,
    params,
    nThreads = opt$cogaps_threads,
    messages = isTRUE(opt$messages),
    outputFrequency = opt$output_frequency,
    checkpointOutFile = checkpoint_path,
    checkpointInterval = opt$checkpoint_interval,
    nSnapshots = opt$n_snapshots,
    snapshotPhase = opt$snapshot_phase,
    asynchronousUpdates = isTRUE(opt$asynchronous_updates)
  )
  saveRDS(result, result_path)

  feature_loadings <- as.matrix(getFeatureLoadings(result))
  sample_factors <- as.matrix(getSampleFactors(result))

  feature_loadings <- ensure_pattern_matrix_orientation(
    mat = feature_loadings,
    expected_rows = nrow(sce),
    expected_names = rownames(sce)
  )
  sample_factors <- ensure_pattern_matrix_orientation(
    mat = sample_factors,
    expected_rows = ncol(sce),
    expected_names = colnames(sce)
  )

  if (is.null(colnames(feature_loadings))) {
    colnames(feature_loadings) <- sprintf("Pattern%d", seq_len(ncol(feature_loadings)))
  } else {
    colnames(feature_loadings) <- canonicalize_pattern_names(colnames(feature_loadings))
  }
  if (is.null(colnames(sample_factors))) {
    colnames(sample_factors) <- sprintf("Pattern%d", seq_len(ncol(sample_factors)))
  } else {
    colnames(sample_factors) <- canonicalize_pattern_names(colnames(sample_factors))
  }

  pat_names <- pattern_columns(colnames(sample_factors))
  if (!"condition" %in% colnames(colData(sce))) {
    stop("The processed H5AD does not contain a 'condition' column in cell metadata.")
  }

  stim_indicator <- as.integer(as.character(colData(sce)$condition) == opt$stim_label)
  pattern_corrs <- vapply(
    pat_names,
    function(pattern) cor(sample_factors[, pattern], stim_indicator),
    numeric(1)
  )
  ifn_pattern <- names(which.max(pattern_corrs))
  ifn_corr <- unname(pattern_corrs[[ifn_pattern]])

  top_genes <- rownames(feature_loadings)[order(feature_loadings[, ifn_pattern], decreasing = TRUE)][seq_len(min(opt$top_genes, nrow(feature_loadings)))]

  runtime_sec <- as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), t0, units = "secs"))
  md <- slot(result, "metadata")

  metrics <- list(
    status = "ok",
    language = "R",
    package = "CoGAPS",
    result_path = basename(result_path),
    nPatterns = opt$k,
    nIterations = opt$n_iter,
    seed = opt$seed,
    sparseOptimization = isTRUE(opt$use_sparse_opt),
    nThreads = opt$cogaps_threads,
    asynchronousUpdates = isTRUE(opt$asynchronous_updates),
    openmpSupport = openmp_support,
    outputFrequency = opt$output_frequency,
    checkpointInterval = opt$checkpoint_interval,
    checkpointOutFile = basename(checkpoint_path),
    nSnapshots = opt$n_snapshots,
    snapshotPhase = opt$snapshot_phase,
    takePumpSamples = isTRUE(opt$take_pump_samples),
    ifn_pattern = ifn_pattern,
    ifn_corr = ifn_corr,
    top_genes = unname(top_genes),
    runtime_sec = runtime_sec,
    totalRunningTime = md$totalRunningTime %||% NA_real_,
    totalUpdates = md$totalUpdates %||% NA_real_,
    meanChiSq = md$meanChiSq %||% NA_real_,
    chisq_trace_length = length(md$chisq %||% numeric()),
    atomsA_trace_length = length(md$atomsA %||% numeric()),
    atomsP_trace_length = length(md$atomsP %||% numeric()),
    equilibrationSnapshots = length(md$equilibrationSnapshotsA %||% list()),
    samplingSnapshots = length(md$samplingSnapshotsA %||% list()),
    pumpStatDim = paste(dim(md$pumpStat %||% matrix(numeric(), nrow = 0, ncol = 0)), collapse = "x"),
    meanPatternAssignmentDim = paste(dim(md$meanPatternAssignment %||% matrix(numeric(), nrow = 0, ncol = 0)), collapse = "x")
  )
  write_metrics(metrics_path, metrics)
}, error = function(e) {
  status <<- "error"
  err_txt <<- conditionMessage(e)
})

if (!identical(status, "ok")) {
  runtime_sec <- as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), t0, units = "secs"))
  write_metrics(
    metrics_path,
    list(
      status = status,
      language = "R",
      package = "CoGAPS",
      nPatterns = opt$k,
      nIterations = opt$n_iter,
      seed = opt$seed,
      sparseOptimization = isTRUE(opt$use_sparse_opt),
      nThreads = opt$cogaps_threads,
      asynchronousUpdates = isTRUE(opt$asynchronous_updates),
      openmpSupport = compiledWithOpenMPSupport(),
      outputFrequency = opt$output_frequency,
      checkpointInterval = opt$checkpoint_interval,
      checkpointOutFile = basename(checkpoint_path),
      nSnapshots = opt$n_snapshots,
      snapshotPhase = opt$snapshot_phase,
      takePumpSamples = isTRUE(opt$take_pump_samples),
      runtime_sec = runtime_sec,
      error = err_txt
    )
  )
  stop(err_txt)
}
5. Export R diagnostic tables

scripts/export_cogaps_diagnostics_r.R
Reads the full selected R CoGAPS object and writes trace, snapshot, uncertainty, pump, and diagnostic files. 

#!/usr/bin/env Rscript

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(optparse)
  library(jsonlite)
  library(zellkonverter)
  library(CoGAPS)
  library(SummarizedExperiment)
})

`%||%` <- function(x, y) if (is.null(x)) y else x

script_arg <- grep("^--file=", commandArgs(trailingOnly = FALSE), value = TRUE)
script_path <- if (length(script_arg) > 0) sub("^--file=", "", script_arg[[1]]) else "."
ROOT <- normalizePath(file.path(dirname(script_path), ".."), winslash = "/", mustWork = TRUE)
default_preprocessed <- file.path(ROOT, "data", "processed", "input", "preprocessed_cells_hvg3000.h5ad")
default_result_rds <- file.path(ROOT, "data", "processed", "selected_model_k6", "r", "cogaps_K6_seed2_iter2000.rds")
default_out_dir <- file.path(ROOT, "data", "processed", "selected_model_k6", "r")

option_list <- list(
  make_option("--preprocessed-h5ad", type = "character", dest = "preprocessed_h5ad", default = default_preprocessed, help = "Processed cells x genes AnnData (.h5ad) [default %default]"),
  make_option("--result-rds", type = "character", dest = "result_rds", default = default_result_rds, help = "Saved CoGAPS R result (.rds) [default %default]"),
  make_option("--outdir", type = "character", default = default_out_dir, help = "Output directory [default %default]"),
  make_option("--top-n", type = "integer", dest = "top_n", default = 15, help = "Top features used in stability summaries [default %default]")
)

opt <- parse_args(OptionParser(option_list = option_list))

PREPROCESSED_H5AD <- opt$preprocessed_h5ad
RESULT_RDS <- opt$result_rds
OUT_DIR <- opt$outdir
TOP_N <- opt$top_n

dir.create(OUT_DIR, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

tag <- sub("^cogaps_(.*)\\.rds$", "\\1", basename(RESULT_RDS))
if (identical(tag, basename(RESULT_RDS))) {
  tag <- tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(RESULT_RDS))
}

pattern_columns <- function(x) {
  pats <- grep("^Pattern_?[0-9]+$", x, value = TRUE)
  pats[order(as.integer(sub("^Pattern_?", "", pats)))]
}

canonicalize_pattern_names <- function(x) {
  sub("^Pattern_?([0-9]+)$", "Pattern\\1", x)
}

ensure_pattern_matrix_orientation <- function(mat, expected_rows, expected_names) {
  if (nrow(mat) != expected_rows && ncol(mat) == expected_rows) {
    mat <- t(mat)
  }
  if (nrow(mat) != expected_rows) {
    stop(sprintf("Unexpected matrix shape. Expected %d rows, got %d.", expected_rows, nrow(mat)))
  }
  if (is.null(rownames(mat))) {
    rownames(mat) <- expected_names
  }
  mat
}

write_gz_tsv <- function(df, path) {
  con <- gzfile(path, open = "wt")
  on.exit(close(con), add = TRUE)
  write.table(df, con, sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)
}

safe_cor <- function(x, y) {
  if (length(x) != length(y) || length(x) < 2) {
    return(NA_real_)
  }
  if (sd(x) == 0 || sd(y) == 0) {
    return(NA_real_)
  }
  suppressWarnings(cor(x, y))
}

top_index_overlap <- function(current, final, n = 15) {
  n <- min(n, length(current), length(final))
  current_top <- names(sort(current, decreasing = TRUE))[seq_len(n)]
  final_top <- names(sort(final, decreasing = TRUE))[seq_len(n)]
  length(intersect(current_top, final_top)) / n
}

param_to_list <- function(params) {
  out <- list()
  for (nm in slotNames(params)) {
    value <- slot(params, nm)
    if (is.null(value)) {
      out[[nm]] <- NULL
    } else if (length(dim(value)) > 0) {
      out[[nm]] <- list(dim = dim(value), class = class(value))
    } else if (is.atomic(value) && length(value) <= 50) {
      out[[nm]] <- unname(value)
    } else {
      out[[nm]] <- list(class = class(value), length = length(value))
    }
  }
  out
}

build_trace_df <- function(md) {
  n <- max(length(md$chisq %||% numeric()), length(md$atomsA %||% numeric()), length(md$atomsP %||% numeric()))
  if (!is.finite(n) || n == 0) {
    return(data.frame())
  }
  fill <- function(x) {
    x <- x %||% numeric()
    c(as.numeric(x), rep(NA_real_, n - length(x)))
  }
  out <- data.frame(
    trace_index = seq_len(n),
    relative_progress = seq_len(n) / n,
    chisq = fill(md$chisq),
    atomsA = fill(md$atomsA),
    atomsP = fill(md$atomsP)
  )
  out$delta_chisq <- c(NA_real_, diff(out$chisq))
  out$delta_atomsA <- c(NA_real_, diff(out$atomsA))
  out$delta_atomsP <- c(NA_real_, diff(out$atomsP))
  out
}

summarize_snapshots <- function(snapshot_list, final_mat, phase, matrix_name, top_n) {
  if (!length(snapshot_list)) {
    return(data.frame())
  }
  final_vec <- as.numeric(final_mat)
  final_norm <- sqrt(sum(final_vec^2))
  do.call(
    rbind,
    lapply(seq_along(snapshot_list), function(i) {
      snap <- snapshot_list[[i]]
      if (!is.null(colnames(snap))) {
        colnames(snap) <- canonicalize_pattern_names(colnames(snap))
      }
      snap_vec <- as.numeric(snap)
      overlap <- NA_real_
      if (identical(matrix_name, "A")) {
        per_pattern_overlap <- vapply(
          colnames(final_mat),
          function(pattern) top_index_overlap(snap[, pattern], final_mat[, pattern], n = top_n),
          numeric(1)
        )
        overlap <- mean(per_pattern_overlap)
      }
      data.frame(
        phase = phase,
        snapshot_label = names(snapshot_list)[i] %||% as.character(i),
        matrix = matrix_name,
        frobenius_to_final = sqrt(sum((snap_vec - final_vec)^2)),
        relative_frobenius_to_final = sqrt(sum((snap_vec - final_vec)^2)) / final_norm,
        correlation_to_final = safe_cor(snap_vec, final_vec),
        nnz = sum(snap_vec > 0),
        mean_top_overlap = overlap,
        row.names = NULL
      )
    })
  )
}

summarize_uncertainty <- function(A, P, A_sd, P_sd, top_n) {
  patterns <- colnames(A)
  do.call(
    rbind,
    lapply(patterns, function(pattern) {
      ordered_genes <- order(A[, pattern], decreasing = TRUE)
      top_idx <- ordered_genes[seq_len(min(top_n, length(ordered_genes)))]
      weight_top <- A[top_idx, pattern]
      sd_top <- A_sd[top_idx, pattern]
      cv_top <- sd_top / pmax(abs(weight_top), 1e-8)
      data.frame(
        pattern = pattern,
        mean_loading_sd = mean(A_sd[, pattern]),
        median_loading_sd = median(A_sd[, pattern]),
        max_loading_sd = max(A_sd[, pattern]),
        mean_factor_sd = mean(P_sd[, pattern]),
        median_factor_sd = median(P_sd[, pattern]),
        max_factor_sd = max(P_sd[, pattern]),
        top_gene_mean_weight = mean(weight_top),
        top_gene_mean_loading_sd = mean(sd_top),
        top_gene_median_loading_cv = median(cv_top),
        row.names = NULL
      )
    })
  )
}

sce <- zellkonverter::readH5AD(PREPROCESSED_H5AD, reader = "R")
result <- readRDS(RESULT_RDS)
md <- slot(result, "metadata")

A <- as.matrix(getFeatureLoadings(result))
P <- as.matrix(getSampleFactors(result))
A_sd <- as.matrix(slot(result, "loadingStdDev"))
P_sd <- as.matrix(slot(result, "factorStdDev"))

A <- ensure_pattern_matrix_orientation(A, nrow(sce), rownames(sce))
P <- ensure_pattern_matrix_orientation(P, ncol(sce), colnames(sce))
A_sd <- ensure_pattern_matrix_orientation(A_sd, nrow(sce), rownames(sce))
P_sd <- ensure_pattern_matrix_orientation(P_sd, ncol(sce), colnames(sce))

if (is.null(colnames(A))) {
  colnames(A) <- sprintf("Pattern%d", seq_len(ncol(A)))
} else {
  colnames(A) <- canonicalize_pattern_names(colnames(A))
}
if (is.null(colnames(P))) {
  colnames(P) <- sprintf("Pattern%d", seq_len(ncol(P)))
} else {
  colnames(P) <- canonicalize_pattern_names(colnames(P))
}
colnames(A_sd) <- colnames(A)
colnames(P_sd) <- colnames(P)

trace_df <- build_trace_df(md)
snapshot_summary <- rbind(
  summarize_snapshots(md$equilibrationSnapshotsA %||% list(), A, "equilibration", "A", TOP_N),
  summarize_snapshots(md$equilibrationSnapshotsP %||% list(), P, "equilibration", "P", TOP_N),
  summarize_snapshots(md$samplingSnapshotsA %||% list(), A, "sampling", "A", TOP_N),
  summarize_snapshots(md$samplingSnapshotsP %||% list(), P, "sampling", "P", TOP_N)
)
uncertainty_summary <- summarize_uncertainty(A, P, A_sd, P_sd, top_n = TOP_N)

if (!is.null(md$pumpStat) && all(dim(md$pumpStat) > 0)) {
  pump_df <- data.frame(gene = rownames(A), md$pumpStat, row.names = NULL, check.names = FALSE)
  colnames(pump_df)[-1] <- colnames(A)
  write_gz_tsv(pump_df, file.path(OUT_DIR, sprintf("cogaps_%s.pump_stat.tsv.gz", tag)))
}

if (!is.null(md$meanPatternAssignment) && all(dim(md$meanPatternAssignment) > 0)) {
  assign_df <- data.frame(gene = rownames(A), md$meanPatternAssignment, row.names = NULL, check.names = FALSE)
  colnames(assign_df)[-1] <- colnames(A)
  write_gz_tsv(assign_df, file.path(OUT_DIR, sprintf("cogaps_%s.mean_pattern_assignment.tsv.gz", tag)))
}

write.csv(trace_df, file.path(OUT_DIR, sprintf("cogaps_%s.trace.csv", tag)), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(snapshot_summary, file.path(OUT_DIR, sprintf("cogaps_%s.snapshot_summary.csv", tag)), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(uncertainty_summary, file.path(OUT_DIR, sprintf("cogaps_%s.pattern_uncertainty_summary.csv", tag)), row.names = FALSE)

diagnostics_summary <- list(
  status = "ok",
  language = "R",
  package = "CoGAPS",
  package_version = as.character(md$version %||% utils::packageVersion("CoGAPS")),
  result_rds = basename(RESULT_RDS),
  dimensions = list(genes = nrow(A), samples = nrow(P), patterns = ncol(A)),
  params = param_to_list(md$params),
  metadata_summary = list(
    meanChiSq = md$meanChiSq %||% NA_real_,
    totalUpdates = md$totalUpdates %||% NA_real_,
    totalRunningTime = md$totalRunningTime %||% NA_real_,
    averageQueueLengthA = md$averageQueueLengthA %||% NA_real_,
    averageQueueLengthP = md$averageQueueLengthP %||% NA_real_,
    chisq_points = length(md$chisq %||% numeric()),
    atomsA_points = length(md$atomsA %||% numeric()),
    atomsP_points = length(md$atomsP %||% numeric()),
    equilibrationSnapshots = length(md$equilibrationSnapshotsA %||% list()),
    samplingSnapshots = length(md$samplingSnapshotsA %||% list()),
    pumpStatDim = dim(md$pumpStat %||% matrix(numeric(), nrow = 0, ncol = 0)),
    meanPatternAssignmentDim = dim(md$meanPatternAssignment %||% matrix(numeric(), nrow = 0, ncol = 0))
  ),
  trace_summary = if (nrow(trace_df)) list(
    chisq_start = trace_df$chisq[1],
    chisq_end = trace_df$chisq[nrow(trace_df)],
    chisq_min = min(trace_df$chisq, na.rm = TRUE),
    chisq_max = max(trace_df$chisq, na.rm = TRUE),
    chisq_num_increases = sum(diff(trace_df$chisq) > 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    chisq_num_decreases = sum(diff(trace_df$chisq) < 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    atomsA_start = trace_df$atomsA[1],
    atomsA_end = trace_df$atomsA[nrow(trace_df)],
    atomsP_start = trace_df$atomsP[1],
    atomsP_end = trace_df$atomsP[nrow(trace_df)]
  ) else NULL
)

write_json(
  diagnostics_summary,
  path = file.path(OUT_DIR, sprintf("cogaps_%s.diagnostics.json", tag)),
  auto_unbox = TRUE,
  pretty = TRUE,
  null = "null"
)

cat("Wrote CoGAPS diagnostics to:", OUT_DIR, "\n")
